intended_object: Per the docstring: given a short complex S in J ⥤ C and cocones c₁, c₂, c₃ on its objects together with compatible maps f, g between their cocone points, the induced short complex c₁.pt ⟶ c₂.pt ⟶ c₃.pt in C. It is an auxiliary packaging used to state colim.exact_mapShortComplex with arbitrary colimit cocones.
explanation: The body is ShortComplex.mk f g, with the zero condition f ≫ g = 0 proved from hc₁.hom_ext: at each j, hf, hg and S.zero give (S.f ≫ S.g).app j ≫ c₃.ι.app j = 0. This is correct. It is not a new mathematical notion. The underlying idea, the image of S under the colimit functor, is already S.map colim in Mathlib. This definition only lets the user plug in arbitrary colimit cocones and compatible maps instead of the chosen colimits. Its sole purpose is to state the exactness lemma colim.exact_mapShortComplex right below it, whose docstring says exactly this. Side remark: the instance variables HasColimitsOfShape J C and HasExactColimitsOfShape J C are presumably pulled into the definition (their types mention only J and C), although the construction does not use them. This is harmless for an auxiliary API device.
